title: Statistical physics of human cooperation
publisher: arXiv (Perc, Jordan, Rand, Wang, Boccaletti, Szolnoki; Physics Reports)

key_points.claim: Review of experimental and theoretical work on human cooperation, focusing on spatial pattern formation, spatiotemporal dynamics and self-organization that promote or hinder social states.
key_points.evidence_quote: focusing on spatial pattern formation, on the spatiotemporal dynamics of observed solutions, and on self-organization that may either promote or hinder socially favorable states.

key_points.claim: Non-equilibrium statistical physics and Monte Carlo methods are the main modelling tools for explaining counterintuitive evolutionary outcomes.
key_points.evidence_quote: Non-equilibrium statistical physics, in particular Monte Carlo methods and the theory of collective behavior of interacting particles near phase transition points, has proven to be very valuable

key_points.claim: Human interactions are group-based with many states, so they are more complex than pairwise particle interactions in physics.
key_points.evidence_quote: interactions among humans often involve group interactions, and they also involve a larger number of possible states

key_points.claim: The review covers incentive mechanisms (peer and pool punishment, rewarding, institutionalized and self-organized incentives, tolerance), with the public goods game as the null model.
key_points.evidence_quote: Public goods game as the null model

reliability_notes: Only the start of the document (abstract and table of contents) was read. It is a peer-reviewed review from a reputable group. It is about lattice and evolutionary-game models, not agent-based artificial societies in general. Claims come from the abstract and table of contents, not from the full text.
